lesson.title: Character Codes
lesson.driving_question: How can a program move between a character and its numeric code?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Converting between individual characters and numeric character codes
lesson.concept_budget: Convert one character with ord() and one valid code with chr(); full-message transformation is deferred to challenges and capstone integration.
misconceptions: chr() accepts a valid whole-number code.
Adding 1 changes the code before chr() converts it back.
Alphabet wraparound needs extra logic and is deferred.
lesson.progression_note: Introduces the character conversion primitives required by the reference robust-programming strand.

shared_program.code:
letter = input("One lower-case letter a-y: ")
code = ord(letter)
next_letter = chr(code + 1)
print("Character code:", code)
print("Next letter:", next_letter)

primm.prompt: Recall that a string may contain one character and that an arithmetic expression is evaluated before its result is passed to a function.
Use d. Trace the stored code, the value after adding 1, and the character returned by chr().
Run with d and then a. Compare the numeric code and next letter. Keep inputs within a-y as instructed.

questions: Why does ord() require exactly one character rather than a whole word?
If you enter c, which number is stored in code?
If you enter c, what does code + 1 do before chr() creates the next letter?
What would be displayed if code + 1 were printed without passing it to chr()?

primm.prompt: Change the input message so it asks for one lower-case letter from b to z. Subtract 1 from [code], pass the result to chr(), and store the returned character in [previous_letter] instead of [next_letter]. Test "d"; display "Previous letter: c".

Ask for one lower-case letter between a and w and store it in [letter]. Ask for a whole number between 1 and 3 and store it in [shift]. Add [shift] to the character code, pass the result to chr(), and store the returned character in [encoded]. Test "c" and 2; display "Encoded letter: e".

Ask for three lower-case letters between a and y. Increase each character code by 1 and pass each result to chr(). Join the three returned characters and store the result in [encoded_text]. Test "a", "b" and "c"; display "Encoded text: bcd".
Repair the ord() argument and pass the changed numeric code into chr().

programs.challenge1:
letter = input("One lower-case letter b-z: ")
code = ord(letter)
previous_letter = chr(code - 1)
print("Character code:", code)
print("Previous letter:", previous_letter)
programs.challenge2:
letter = input("One lower-case letter a-w: ")
shift = int(input("Shift 1 to 3: "))
code = ord(letter)
encoded = chr(code + shift)
print("Encoded letter:", encoded)
programs.challenge3:
first = input("First letter a-y: ")
second = input("Second letter a-y: ")
third = input("Third letter a-y: ")
encoded_first = chr(ord(first) + 1)
encoded_second = chr(ord(second) + 1)
encoded_third = chr(ord(third) + 1)
encoded_text = encoded_first + encoded_second + encoded_third
print("Encoded text:", encoded_text)
